rows.source: Building Safety Regulator mandatory occurrence service
rows.verified: The service defines an in-scope higher-risk building as at least 7 storeys or at least 18 metres high together with the relevant use criteria.

rows.source: Building Safety Regulator mandatory occurrence service
rows.verified: The use criteria include at least 2 residential units or a hospital or care home.

rows.source: BSR mandatory occurrence guidance
rows.verified: Reportable safety occurrences include structural failure incidents and risks.

rows.source: BSR mandatory occurrence guidance
rows.verified: During design and construction, reportable occurrences include fire-safety incidents and risks.

rows.source: BSR mandatory occurrence guidance
rows.verified: During occupation, reportable occurrences include spread of fire or smoke in the building.

rows.source: Building Safety Regulator mandatory occurrence service
rows.verified: The reporting threshold includes occurrences causing or likely to risk the death of a significant number of people.

rows.source: Building Safety Regulator mandatory occurrence service
rows.verified: The threshold includes serious injury requiring immediate hospital treatment or permanent disabling harm to a significant number of people.

rows.source: Building Safety Regulator mandatory occurrence service
rows.verified: Safety occurrences include both incidents that happened and risks of future incidents.

rows.source: Building Safety Regulator mandatory occurrence service
rows.verified: A qualifying safety occurrence generally remains reportable even if it is remedied immediately.

rows.source: Building Safety Regulator mandatory occurrence service
rows.verified: Accountable persons, principal accountable persons, principal contractors and principal designers can have reporting duties.

rows.source: Building Safety Regulator mandatory occurrence service
rows.verified: A mandatory occurrence notice must be submitted as soon as possible after identification and before the full report.

rows.source: Building Safety Regulator mandatory occurrence service
rows.verified: The mandatory occurrence report must be submitted within 10 calendar days of identifying the occurrence.

rows.source: Building Safety Regulator mandatory occurrence service
rows.verified: BSR provides a notice reference number that is used for the subsequent report.

rows.source: Building Safety Regulator mandatory occurrence service
rows.verified: The notice records the occurrence description, identification time and immediate actions taken to keep people safe.

rows.source: BSR mandatory occurrence system guidance
rows.verified: Principal designers and principal contractors must establish the reporting system before building work begins and operate it through the project.

rows.source: BSR mandatory occurrence system guidance
rows.verified: The principal accountable person must establish and operate a single mandatory occurrence reporting system for the occupied high-rise residential building.

rows.source: BSR mandatory occurrence system guidance
rows.verified: The mandatory occurrence reporting system must be reviewed regularly so it remains effective.

rows.source: BSR mandatory occurrence guidance
rows.verified: Whether potential harm affects a significant number of people requires dutyholder assessment against the statutory criteria.

rows.source: BSR mandatory occurrence guidance
rows.verified: Fire-safety reporting scope differs between design/construction and occupation, so the building phase must be identified.

rows.source: Building Safety Regulator mandatory occurrence reporting
rows.verified: Mandatory occurrence records are building- and event-specific and are not converted into parcel-level safety probability.
